description: Every way an arrow can be drawn, over a colour bed and with nothing on disk. Top: a straight arrow running right, head at the end only. Middle: an S-curve between two levels — it leaves its start horizontally and arrives horizontally, and its head is aimed along the curve's own tangent, so a head that came out pointing along the straight line between the ends is visibly askew here and nowhere else. Bottom left: a double-headed straight arrow, the no-direction case. Bottom right: a plain line, `heads: none`, which is the whole reason `line` is not an outline of its own. What a wrong render looks like: a head at the wrong end means `from` and `to` were crossed; a head on the S pointing down-right instead of right means the tangent was taken from the chord; a fifth arrow anywhere means `heads: none` drew one anyway.
